newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican police and protesters clash, 38 hurt.
newsitem.headline: Mexican police and protesters clash, 38 hurt.

text.p: Thirty-eight people were hurt on Thursday when police clashed with street vendors as they tried to dislodge the merchants from their long-time home in a Mexico City suburb, police said.

The city government of Naucalpan was attempting to remove the street vendors from a site they had occupied for 19 years, but the street vendors resisted, the television news programme 24 Hours reported.
About 150 police in riot gear were forced to resort to force against an unknown number of protesters, 24 Hours said.
"Of the injured, 33 are merchants, and there are five members of the municipal police injured," police detective Miguel Angel Morales Montes told 24 Hours.
One of the street vendors suffered "injuries that put his life in danger," Morales said.
Jose Luis Duran, mayor of Naucalpan, which is just northwest of Mexico City, said police were acting in self-defence.
Following the breakup, about 200 supporters of the street vendors set up a protest on the steps of City Hall, the television report said.
